activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type II Regions

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type II Region Given a Diagram
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/fc19dd4415663ab027e0fc386d4c5bc81a28c1bc26d5f6cf2083f4f4228a4dea.png)

 

Evaluate the triple integral 
$\displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 12z^2 \: \mathrm{d}V$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
examples.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/f25c393f10c35ffd9b4fa91cdf672a516cf6cff974a8aa563d350619a64b79bd.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 3-y-z \big\},
$$

where

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/145f0d494ffe24de84e3a289b3a7316d3f4933f193d734aed118609f7fb9f94f.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 3-y-z \big\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
\iiint \limits_{R}  12z^2  \: \textrm{d}V 
= 
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{3-y-z}  12z^2  \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-y-z}12{z}^{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3-y-z}12{z}^{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}12{z}^{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=3-y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}12{z}^{2}(3-y-z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(36{z}^{2}-12y{z}^{2}-12{z}^{3})\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[12{z}^{3}-4y{z}^{3}-3{z}^{4}]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12-4y-3)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9-4y)\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(9-4y)\,dy & =[9y-2{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(9-2)-0 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,0\le x\le yz},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the line $y=1$ and the parabola $z={y}^{2}$ in the first quadrant.
feedback.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{yz}2x\,dx]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{yz}2x\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=yz}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}(yz)^{2}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/acb173db9d28ed8b38e63c7bc365c20e5755aeb1af3f6340e7b9229a4b49101d.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}{z}^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z={y}^{2}}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}({y}^{6}-0)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3}{y}^{8}\,dy \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{1}{9}{y}^{9}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{9}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{27}\end{aligned}
$$
